MEASURED HERE with mwccarm 2004/b56 on this TU, two source forms, one compile each, reading the object's .text section order by section index (never st_value -- mwccarm gives every function its own section, so st_value is 0 for all of them): (1) default deferred codegen with the members in reverse-ROM source order emits [D1, D0, func_ov002_020b6074, _ZN7Vector3D1Ev, func_ov002_020b60fc, Render, Behavior, func_ov002_020b6244, func_ov002_020b62cc, func_ov002_020b6374] -- the seven licensed members in ROM-ascending order with the pair at the head; (2) a defer_codegen off pragma before the members emits [func_ov002_020b6374, func_ov002_020b62cc, _ZN7Vector3D1Ev, func_ov002_020b6244, Behavior, Render, func_ov002_020b60fc, func_ov002_020b6074, D1, D0] -- the members reversed and the pair moved to the tail. The pragma moves the pair between the head and the tail of the object and reverses the seven real members, but THE PAIR'S INTERNAL ORDER IS D1-THEN-D0 IN BOTH. Form (1) is the one shipped, because it is the one whose licensed members come out ROM-ascending. This reproduces on this class what ov002/daObjKaitendai_c measured over four forms on its own identical D0-below-D1 arrangement.

THE ONE FORM THAT WOULD EMIT D0 FIRST IS REFUTED BY THE CARTRIDGE. An out-of-line destructor definition emits the D2/D0/D1 group instead, and no _ZN15daObjGuragura_cD2Ev exists anywhere in config/**/symbols.txt -- the cartridge never carried one for this class. It is ruled out independently of that too: the tree-wide relocation census finds _ZN15daObjGuragura_cD0Ev (0x020b5fd8) named by EXACTLY ONE word in the image, ov002 0x021090c8, and _ZN15daObjGuragura_cD1Ev (0x020b6030) by exactly one, ov002 0x021090c4. Those two words are slots 17 and 16 of _ZTV15daObjGuragura_c (address point 0x02109084; 0x021090c4 - 0x02109084 = 0x40 = slot 16, 0x021090c8 - 0x02109084 = 0x44 = slot 17). No instruction anywhere in the ROM calls either destructor -- both referrers are kind:load into a vtable, neither is an arm_call -- and both descendants inline this destructor's vptr store instead, which the compiler can only do from a body visible in include/daObjGuragura_c.h. An out-of-line definition here would make daObjKm2_Gura_c and daObjFl_Gura_c emit a branch-and-link the cartridge does not have and break their already-matched TUs. This is the same disposition already taken by ov002/daObjFloatBoard_c and ov002/daObjKaitendai_c, whose destructor pairs sit in the identical D0-below-D1 arrangement.

NO FORCING FUNCTION AND NO PRAGMA. The two legacy destructor shards each carried a scaffold (a delete-expression, an explicit destructor call) whose only job was to drag an out-of-line copy into a one-function object. This TU owns the key function, so _ZTV15daObjGuragura_c is emitted here and its slots 16 and 17 odr-use D1 and D0 with nothing added to the source; src/_ZN15daObjGuragura_cD0Ev.cpp and src/_ZN15daObjGuragura_cD1Ev.cpp keep their own per-function delinks entries and this object's copies are licensed as deadstrip-duplicate against those ROM homes.

THREE PREVIOUSLY UNATTRIBUTED FUNCTIONS ARE FOLDED IN BEYOND WHAT build/tu_map.json COULD SEE. func_ov002_020b6244 is this class's shared setup half, reached by an ordinary call from each leaf's own InitResources rather than through a vtable slot, because the class is abstract in slots 0 and 3. func_ov002_020b6374 is the dBgW callback that setup installs, and func_ov002_020b62cc is the body that callback forwards to; each is named by exactly one word in the whole image, and both of those words lie inside this run. tu_map cannot see any of the three: none carries a mangled name or a vtable slot, so no label bounds the run on the right.

The class is ABSTRACT: vtable slots 0 (InitResources) and 3 (CleanupResources) are bare zero words with no relocation, and each of the two leaves supplies its own 0x14-byte InitResources/CleanupResources that loads the shared helper and tail-calls it. There is no factory and no g_profile row in ov002 for this class, which is why the entry claims no data, no ctor and no BSS.

func_ov002_020b6074, func_ov002_020b60fc, func_ov002_020b6244, func_ov002_020b62cc and func_ov002_020b6374 keep their address-derived names. None occupies a vtable slot in any class in the image and nothing in the ROM names any of them, so a coined English name would be invention, not recovery.

ONE SOURCE-LEVEL CHANGE WAS FORCED BY THE LANGUAGE MODE, and it is byte-neutral: src/func_ov002_020b6244.c declared the fourth parameter of _ZN10dBgW_KcMbg7SetFileEP8KCL_FileRK9Matrix4x35Fix12IiEsR10CLPS_Block through a file-local typedef of Fix12 to int. Fix12 is a class template in include/types.h, so in a C++ TU that typedef is a redefinition and mwccarm rejects it (typename redefined). The parameter is spelled int directly instead -- what the mangled name's by-value Fix12<int> lowers to, and the spelling the matched sibling ov002/daObjKaitendai_c already uses for the same call. All seven members match after the change.

POST-PROMOTION tubuild.py linkcheck IS STRUCTURALLY UNAVAILABLE TO THIS ENTRY, and that is not a defect in it. Once the single intact delinks.txt entry exists, linkcheck treats the source as an enrolled intact-object candidate and routes its object through tools/tu_production.prepare_intact_object, which refuses any entry that does not claim a non-text section: intact production requires one .text claim and at least one non-text claim. This TU claims .text only, because the class has no factory, no g_profile row and no owned data.
